Prediction intervals for every child of a benchmark cohort

Source: R/pred.R
wgh_benchmark_intervals.Rd

Applies wgh_prediction_interval() to the full-data fit of a linear or mixed model of a benchmark, for every child of the cohort, and reports whether each observed height falls inside its interval. The coverage is in sample, so it is slightly optimistic. Cross-validated accuracy is in the benchmark's performance table.

Usage

wgh_benchmark_intervals(benchmark, model = "M5", level = 0.95)

Arguments

benchmark

A wgh_benchmark object.

model

Model code (a linear or mixed model, for example "M5").

level

Interval level.

Value

A tibble with one row per child: id, sex, observed, fit, lower, upper, width and covered, with a summary by sex as attribute "summary".

Examples

# \donttest{
pc <- wgh_prediction_cohort(wgh_simulate(8000, seed = 4)$visits)
bm <- wgh_benchmark(pc, models = c("M1", "M5"), folds = 3)
iv <- wgh_benchmark_intervals(bm, "M5")
attr(iv, "summary")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   sex        n mean_width coverage
#>   <chr>  <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Female    84       16.2    0.952
#> 2 Male      58       11.2    0.983
# }
